name: Blend2D
workload: Render time per frame (ms) for the Tiger SVG (960x1014, 301 layers) and the Paris-30k map (4222x3474, 50681 layers) drawn into an RGBA buffer, in a harness that includes Blend2D and Skia; the Blend2D author's own suite also compares AGG, Cairo and Qt with 8x8 to 256x256 render calls.
claimed_speedup: Tiger: Blend2D 0.8 ms vs Skia 5.9 ms (about 7x, derived from page data); Paris-30k: Blend2D 47 ms vs Skia 190 ms (about 4x, derived from page data). A July 2025 Linebender benchmark on Apple M1 Pro reports Blend2D as the clear winner over Skia, Cairo, AGG, Tiny Skia, Vello CPU and JUCE (snippet only, no per-case numbers seen).
hardware: Apple M1 Max, 10 cores (Blaze author's run; 500 runs per image, 5 best and 5 worst dropped); Apple M1 Pro (Linebender run)
tradeoffs: CPU-only (no GPU backend). JIT pipeline generation needs AsmJit (README describes it as the dependency that enables JIT). Per the VGCPU-Benchmark README its coverage model sums subpath coverage and saturates at 1.0 instead of computing exact union, so self-overlapping paths can render differently from Skia and Cairo. Multi-threaded rendering is opt-in through the context creation info.
caveats: Snippet only: the numbers above came from WebSearch result text describing the Blaze author's article (gasiulis.name/parallel-rasterization-on-cpu, blocked here, not opened); the official blend2d.com/performance.html page is also blocked here and was not opened, and the Linebender blog (linebender.org/blog/tmil-19) was not opened. In the Blaze harness (github.com/aurimasg/blaze/tree/master/Benchmarks, opened) Blend2D is created with threadCount equal to the hardware thread count while Skia uses a single-threaded raster canvas, so the Skia ratio mixes multi-threaded and single-threaded runs. Compiler and flags are not stated in what was seen. A 2020 HN snippet (news.ycombinator.com item 25076872) says Blend2D is still slower than Skia in some cases; the repo's own README has no benchmark numbers and the repo issue 'Performance Comparison' (blend2d/blend2d issue 3) contains none either. The bl_bench tool repo (blend2d/blend2d-apps) returned 404 twice. Note Blend2D is itself one of the listed baselines; it is recorded because it claims to beat Skia and Cairo.
found_via: WebSearch: 'Blend2D performance benchmark vs Cairo Skia Qt AGG rendering time per operation'; github.com/topics/2d-graphics?l=c%2B%2B; Blaze author article snippet

name: ThorVG
workload: Frames per second drawing 5,000 semi-transparent primitives (rects, rotated rects, strokes, circles, PNG images, gradients) with alpha blending at 2560x1440 on the CPU backend, ThorVG v1.1 vs Skia v148, using the thorvg.benchmark app.
claimed_speedup: README: average ~2.9x faster than Skia on CPU. Per-case fps from the README chart image (ThorVG vs Skia): Rects 76.0 vs 17.2 (4.4x); Rotated Rects 36.0 vs 10.1 (3.6x); Stroke 55.7 vs 17.2 (3.2x); Rects+Stroke 41.8 vs 10.5 (4.0x); Rotated Rects+Stroke 25.0 vs 4.5 (5.6x); Circles 38.5 vs 10.4 (3.7x); Images (PNG) 6.4 vs 6.0 (1.1x); Rotated Images 4.4 vs 4.4 (1.0x); Linear Gradient 9.0 vs 8.5 (1.1x); Radial Gradient 6.9 vs 6.0 (1.2x).
compiler_and_flags: Benchmark harness built with CMake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release; ThorVG built with meson -Dloaders=all -Dengines=all; Skia installed through vcpkg (config not stated); compiler version not stated
stars_or_usage: 1.9k stars; used by Canva (Lottie), SEGGER, Lottie Creator per README
tradeoffs: Smaller feature set than Skia (core binary about 170KB per README); focused on SVG and Lottie, with software, OpenGL and WebGPU backends. Per the VGCPU-Benchmark README its CPU rasterizer uses a sum-then-saturate coverage model (not exact union), so self-overlapping paths can differ from Skia and Cairo. The gain is large for rect, stroke and circle workloads but only 1.0x to 1.2x for images and gradients.
caveats: First-party benchmark from the ThorVG maintainers. The per-case numbers were read from the chart image (thorvg.site repo, readme/example_performance.png, fetched through raw.githubusercontent.com) that the README displays; the README text itself states only the ~2.9x average and the test conditions. The benchmark code is public (github.com/thorvg/thorvg.benchmark, opened, MIT) but compiler and flags are not stated, so this is C, not A. Skia comes from a vcpkg build with unknown options; Skia CPU raster is single-threaded while ThorVG has an optional task-scheduler thread pool and the benchmark setup installs libomp, thread counts are not stated. The maintainers' own discussion (github.com/orgs/thorvg/discussions/1815, opened) quotes outside criticism that Blend2D beats ThorVG's software renderer significantly and says no formal Blend2D comparison existed at that time, so there is no evidence ThorVG beats Blend2D.
found_via: GitHub: github.com/topics/2d-graphics?l=c%2B%2B; github.com/topics/vector-graphics?l=c%2B%2B; WebSearch 'SVG renderer speed comparison benchmark lunasvg plutosvg thorvg resvg'

name: Blaze
workload: Render time per frame (ms) for Tiger (960x1014, 301 layers) and Paris-30k (4222x3474, 50681 layers) vector scenes into an RGBA buffer, 500 runs per image with the 5 best and 5 worst removed.
claimed_speedup: Tiger: Blaze 0.6 ms vs Blend2D 0.8 ms vs Skia 5.9 ms (about 9.8x vs Skia and 1.3x vs Blend2D, derived from page data); Paris-30k: Blaze 18 ms vs Blend2D 47 ms vs Skia 190 ms (about 10.6x vs Skia and 2.6x vs Blend2D, derived from page data).
tradeoffs: Multi-threaded, CPU-only rasterizer; needs POSIX threads (no Windows support yet per README, and it needs fast bit-count and trailing-zero intrinsics); demos for WebAssembly (Emscripten with SharedArrayBuffer) and macOS. It is a rasterizer core, not a full drawing API.
caveats: Snippet only: the numbers came from WebSearch result text summarizing the author's article (gasiulis.name/parallel-rasterization-on-cpu, linked from the README, blocked here, not opened). The benchmark code is public in the repo (Benchmarks/ with Benchmark.cpp, BenchmarkBlaze.cpp, BenchmarkBlend2D.cpp, BenchmarkSkia.cpp, BenchmarkCoreGraphics.cpp; opened, and it confirms RunCount=500 with 5 best and 5 worst dropped), but compiler and flags are not stated. In the harness Blend2D uses threadCount equal to the hardware thread count while the Skia canvas (SkCanvas::MakeRasterDirect, anti-alias on) is single-threaded, so the Skia ratio compares a multi-threaded rasterizer with a single-threaded one. Author-run comparison of his own project. Last commit 2024-09-30.
found_via: WebSearch: 'faster than Blend2D OR faster than Skia CPU vector graphics rasterizer C++ library github'; github.com/topics/vector-graphics?l=c%2B%2B

name: tiny-skia-cpp
workload: 512x512 FillRect and FillPath rendering, C++ SIMD backend vs the Rust tiny-skia implementation, normalized to Rust = 1.0x (ARM measured on Apple Silicon NEON, x86 on Intel/AMD with AVX2+FMA).
claimed_speedup: Up to 1.9x faster than Rust tiny-skia: FillRect ARM 1.9x, x86 1.3x; FillPath ARM 1.4x, x86 1.2x; SIMD speedup over the C++ scalar backend up to 2.3x (x86 AVX2) and 1.9x (ARM NEON).
hardware: Apple Silicon (NEON) and Intel/AMD (AVX2+FMA), exact CPU models not stated
tradeoffs: CPU-only C++20 port of the Skia-subset algorithms with x86-64 AVX2+FMA and ARM64 NEON backends plus a scalar fallback, zero dependencies, Bazel or CMake. Output is near-pixel-accurate against Rust tiny-skia, not bit-exact (extra analytic AA and filter primitives). Only a subset of Skia features.
caveats: The baseline is the Rust port, not Skia, Cairo or Blend2D, so this does not show it beats those. A WebSearch snippet of the Rust tiny-skia docs (not opened) says tiny-skia is 20-100% slower than Skia on x86-64 and 100-300% slower on ARM, which means the C++ port is likely still not faster than Skia itself. Only two workloads at one size, CPU models and compiler flags not stated; the repo has benchmark code (tests/benchmarks with RenderPerfBench.cpp and run_render_perf_compare.sh, which compare C++ SIMD, C++ scalar and Rust via FFI) so the claim is reproducible but missing methodology. Repo is small and recent with a bot commit as the latest.

name: Rive Renderer (rive-runtime)
baseline: Skia (and Flutter Impeller) rendering Rive content
workload: Animated vector tiles drawn on an iPhone 12 (many path-heavy tiles per frame), Rive Renderer vs Skia/Impeller.
claimed_speedup: Snippet only: 66x faster, 6000 tiles/sec vs 90 tiles/sec; in one test Skia rendered 9 tiles at about 100 ms (10 fps) while the Rive Renderer rendered 100 tiles at about 16 ms (60 fps).
stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars; the renderer behind Rive runtimes
tradeoffs: GPU renderer (Metal, Vulkan, D3D12, D3D11, OpenGL/WebGL, per the README) built around a geometric reduction of anti-aliased paths into triangle patches and best with pixel local storage support; not a CPU rasterizer. Designed for Rive content and its runtime, with an abstract renderer interface (a Skia integration layer and a CoreGraphics renderer also exist in the repo).
caveats: Vendor claim from Rive's own marketing: numbers came from WebSearch snippets of a LinkedIn post by a Rive employee and Rive's blog (rive.app, blocked here and not opened). The repo README makes no performance claim and publishes no numbers; it only mentions a bench binary (out/<config>/bench). A 66x ratio on a hand-picked many-tile animation scenario is over the 50x plausibility line, so it is capped at C. The search snippet itself says benchmarking is difficult and depends heavily on hardware pixel local storage support. No compiler or flags stated.
found_via: WebSearch: 'Rive renderer vs Skia performance benchmark rive-runtime path rendering faster'

name: vkvg
baseline: Cairo (GL ES3 backend) and Skia (Vulkan backend)
workload: vgperf, a caskbench-style C harness, drawing lines/strokes, rectangles, circles and stars with vkvg (Vulkan), Cairo (GL es3) and Skia (Vulkan).
claimed_speedup: Chart only (y-axis has no label or unit, probably time per frame where lower is better); approximate bar values read from the chart image (derived from page data): lines stroke vkvg ~0.00013, cairo es3 ~0.0031, skia ~0.0004; rectangles ~0.00025, ~0.00025, ~0.0002; circles vkvg ~0.00065, cairo ~0.0035, skia ~0.00016; stars vkvg ~0.00058, cairo ~0.0019, skia ~0.00062. So vkvg beats Cairo es3 on 3 of 4 tests and ties on rectangles; it beats Skia only on lines stroke and loses clearly on circles.
compiler_and_flags: Skia built with gn args is_official_build=true is_component_build=true skia_use_vulkan=true (vgperf README); vkvg and Cairo flags not stated
tradeoffs: Needs Vulkan; GPU-only; Cairo-like C API; alpha-stage per README; fill (stencil even-odd and non-zero), stroke, gradients, dashes and a font system with caching are implemented.
caveats: First-party chart with no axis label, unit, GPU or CPU model, run count or Cairo/vkvg versions, so the numbers are approximate readings of a PNG and the metric direction is inferred. vgperf (5 stars, 22 commits, MIT) has no numeric results, only the chart; Skia was built from a patched experimental C API branch. Only 4 simple drawing tests. Mixed result against Skia. Cairo is measured through its GL ES3 backend, not its image (CPU) backend.

name: LunaSVG
baseline: cairosvg 2.9.1 (Python, renders through Cairo 1.18.4) and resvg-py 0.5.0
workload: Median time per icon, SVG bytes to PNG bytes, for 3,460 simple-icons SVGs (24x24 viewBox) scaled to 256 px and 1024 px, plus 943 resvg feature-test SVGs (filters and text excluded), through the pillow-lunasvg Python binding of LunaSVG 3.5.0.
claimed_speedup: simple-icons at 256 px: 1.00 ms vs cairosvg 2.17 ms (2.2x) and resvg-py 2.84 ms (2.8x); at 1024 px: 12.56 ms vs cairosvg 23.63 ms (1.9x) and resvg-py 34.85 ms (2.8x); render-only without PNG encode 0.11 ms at 256 px and 0.88 ms at 1024 px; resvg tests at 1024 px: 5.26 ms vs 19.16 ms cairosvg and 27.22 ms resvg-py.
compiler_and_flags: pillow-lunasvg 0.1.0 built locally from commit 653c187 (LunaSVG 3.5.0), Python 3.13.15, Pillow 12.3.0; C++ compiler and flags not stated; exact commands are in the results file
stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars; embedded in many apps, pillow-lunasvg wheels on PyPI
tradeoffs: Lightweight SVG 1.1/Tiny 1.2 renderer on top of the plutovg rasterizer. No filters, no SVG inside <image>, no WebP images, no CSS transform property, no transform-origin, no mix-blend-mode, no context-fill. Only 59% of resvg's feature tests match resvg output at 1% pixel tolerance (cairosvg 53%).
caveats: Independent third-party measurement (by the author of the pillow-lunasvg wrapper, who also had a PR merged in the LunaSVG README on 2026-09-17), measured through a Python wrapper, so the time includes Pillow load and PNG encode (most of the 1.00 ms) and the baselines are Python wrappers, not Cairo or Skia directly. resvg filter tests are excluded from timing because LunaSVG does not implement filters, and files a renderer rejected are dropped from its numbers. This is an SVG-to-PNG pipeline benchmark rather than a pure rasterizer comparison; closest listed baseline relation is Cairo via cairosvg. Benchmark repo has 0 stars; compiler flags not stated, so B rather than A.
